title: guv-calcs v0.10.0: An open-source Python library for modeling germicidal UV in indoor environments
description:
guv-calcs is an open-source Python scientific computing library for physically based modeling of germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) light in indoor environments, with a focus on far-UVC (200–235 nm) applications. The library provides core numerical tools for representing lamps, spatial geometry, calculation planes and volumes, and exposure metrics such as irradiance, fluence rate, and cumulative dose.

The package implements vectorized radiative transfer calculations using measured photometric data (IES/ULD files), supports flexible three-dimensional room geometries, and is designed for integration with higher-level tools such as visualization dashboards, airflow models, and risk frameworks for airborne pathogen control. The codebase emphasizes reproducibility, transparency, and modularity so that researchers, engineers, and manufacturers can inspect, extend, and validate the underlying calculations.

guv-calcs forms the computational backbone of the broader Illuminate ecosystem, but is usable as a standalone library for custom analyses, batch simulations, and method development. The project aims to improve rigor and accessibility in far-UVC modeling by providing a free, auditable, and community-maintained alternative to proprietary software.

v0.10.0 Release Notes

Added

  • SurfaceGrid.coords_full and values_to_full_grid, matching VolumeGrid; values_to_full_grid takes a `fill` value (default -inf)

Changed

  • A CalcPoint created without `calc_mode` or `horiz` defaults to cosine weighting (planar_normal), like a cosine-corrected radiometer facing its aim point, instead of planar_max; saved points keep their stored flags

Fixed

  • A CalcPoint's field of view is centered on its aim direction. It was applied as a band around the plane perpendicular to the aim (the horizon band of an upward-facing eye plane), so a point aimed at a lamp could miss it and see one well off to the side instead, and the horizontal FOV searched for the brightest direction rather than the aimed one. Points with a full 180/360 field of view are unaffected
  • Reflected light ignored view mode: a zone with view_direction or view_target (eye_directional, eye_target, and now every CalcPoint) filtered light bounced off surfaces by the band around its own plane rather than by its view-centered FOV. Zones without view mode are unaffected
  • README examples that no longer ran: `Room(floor_polygon=...)` is `Room(polygon=...)`, a work plane is built with `CalcPlane.from_polygon`, and a safety check reports `result.status`
  • A saved lamp with a preset_id but no embedded photometry (a hand-edited file, or one written by another tool) loaded without photometry and was silently left out of calculations; it now reloads the bundled preset's IES file and spectrum, keeping its saved placement and scaling. Room.calculate() warns about each enabled lamp it leaves out for missing photometry
  • A disabled lamp came back enabled after save and load: Lamp.to_dict always wrote enabled=True
  • Polygon rooms: exporting a calculation plane (zone.export(), Room.export_zip()) raised ValueError and plot_plane raised TypeError, and polygon volumes exported blank grids under a wrong size header; planes and volumes now export and plot on their full bounding grid, blank (CSV) or NaN (plot) outside the outline
  • Changing one reflective surface's resolution (set_reflectance_num_points / set_reflectance_spacing on a single wall) crashed the next calculate() with a shape mismatch, and moving an object left stale occlusion in reflected light until a hard recalculation: the surface cache compared against zone and scene state that compute() had already updated
  • Changing a zone's FOV or weighting flags (fov_vert, fov_horiz, vert, horiz, use_normal, view_direction, view_target) didn't recompute its reflected values until a hard recalculation
